items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1978-12-03
items.q: Leslie and I drove down to New Orleans

ctx.x: Okay. There was a music store in 3-4th, formed by Bubba Broyles. Bubba was a trumpet player, and he'd been playing with the local bands there. And, he was a great friend of Mr. A.J. LaCoste, who was a power with the Whirland Organization. A.J. was the management of the band department. He organized school bands all over Mississippi and Louisiana. He was a tremendous man. But, Bubba and LaCoste asked me to come to New Orleans, that I would have some kind of a job. I had, I tried to go back to playing and played…
You have to be careful. Now you were talking about Leslie Nurse, was his name?

Yeah. Leslie and Bill Nurse were two brothers. One played piano and one played banjo. They had a little band in the street, but their parents had moved to New Orleans. My father was a Presbyterian minister, and so Leslie and I drove down to New Orleans, and Johnny Grant, who was a drummer from Straitford, had a room at 327 Bourbon Street. It was a rooming house. He offered me an opportunity to stay with him. I didn't have to pay any of that. I landed in New Orleans for eight dollars, and I planned that in the…
